# Revit tool catalogue

<!-- GENERATED by tools/generate-tool-catalogue.py from the cards in brain/fragments and the ribbon code in revit/. Do not edit: run the tool. -->

**Every tool Heron has for Revit, by job** - what each one does, how you reach it, what it needs, what you get, and on which Revit releases it is built and proved. It is written by a script from Heron's own tool cards, so no count or status on these pages is typed by a person.

Heron holds **619 live tools**: **490 are usable in a chat**, 44 are not proved yet but run because they change nothing in the model, and 85 are refused until they are proved. 135 retired tools are left out - each one's card names the tool that replaced it.

## How you reach a tool

**Almost every tool is reached by asking in a Claude chat, not by a button.** Like typing a command in Revit instead of hunting for it on the ribbon: you say what you want - *"which views have no template?"*, *"select all ducts on Level 2"* - and Heron picks the tool whose words match, runs it inside Revit and reports back. The phrases on each page are the ones the tool's card declares; your own words work too.

Before the first request: Revit open with a model, and Heron connected - press **Heron** on the Heron tab until its heron turns orange. Installing Heron: [the installation guide](install.md).

**A request you repeat** can be saved and run again from the **Commands** panel (Heron button's drop-down › Commands) - [Using Heron](using-heron.md).

## The Heron tab in Revit

Read out of the add-in's own ribbon code, so it is what Revit shows:

**Heron tab › AI Bridge panel** - the AI Bridge connector (`revit/Heron.Revit.Addin/HeronApplication.cs`):

| Button | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Heron** (a button with a drop-down arrow) | Connect Heron to this Revit. Orange heron: connected. Click again to disconnect. |
| › Bridge Status (in its drop-down) | See whether Heron is connected to this Revit. |
| › Free this model (in its drop-down) | Let another chat use the model in front now. |
| › Commands (in its drop-down) | Show or hide your saved Heron commands. |
| › Activity (in its drop-down) | Show or hide Heron's recent changes, with Select, Zoom and Undo. |
| **Settings** | Turn Heron's switches on or off: Changes, Admin, Publish, Ask to Keep, Ask to Delete, Companion. |
| **Companion** | Open the Companion page in your browser. It only shows, never changes. |

Not on a modeller's ribbon: the All tools product's **Heron** tab, **Tools** panel (`revit/Heron.Tools/HeronToolsApplication.cs`); the Heron Doc product's **Heron Doc** tab, **Proof** panel (`revit/Heron.Doc/HeronDocApplication.cs`). Each is a `PROVING` product in `platform/heron-products.json` - a shape proof with one button that does nothing - and the installer does not offer it.

## What the status words mean

| Status | What it means for you |
|---|---|
| **Usable in a chat** | Proved on a real Revit model, and its proof still matches its code (D-30). A chat runs it. |
| **DRAFT, runs** / **STALE, runs** | Not proved, or its proof is out of date - but it only reads the model or changes what is shown (a selection, a zoom), so a chat still runs it and the answer says DRAFT. Nothing in the model changes. |
| **Refused until proved** | It would change the model and is not proved, or its proof is out of date. **Not yet usable in a chat - refused until proved (D-117).** |

And what each tool needs switched on:

| Kind | Needs, in Heron's Settings |
|---|---|
| Answers a question (`READ`, `ANALYZE`, `SUGGEST`) | nothing - works with Changes off |
| Changes only what Revit shows (`EXECUTE`) | nothing - works with Changes off |
| Changes the model (`MODIFY`) | **Changes** on |
| Writes files outside the model (`PUBLISH`) | **Changes** and **Publish** on |
| Changes project-wide settings (`ADMIN`) | **Changes** and **Admin** on |

Heron starts with every switch off, so it only reads until you turn **Changes** on. A change is one entry in Revit's Undo list; with **Ask to Keep** on, Revit asks **Keep or Discard** before anything is kept. More: [What keeps the model safe](safety.md).

**Built for** is the Revit releases a tool is compiled for. **Proved on** is the releases a real run was recorded on. A release in the first list and not the second is expected to work and has not been watched working.

## Keeping this page true

It is written by `python tools/generate-tool-catalogue.py` from `brain/fragments/*/fragment.yaml` and the ribbon code in `revit/`, and `python tests/test_tool_catalogue.py` fails when a card changed and the pages were not written again. Change a card, then run the tool.
